prd_accuracy.rationale: The public PRD describes ymlcodec as a JavaScript YAML 1.2 parser and writer with optional YAML 1.1 types. Feature points FP-01 through FP-07 map one-to-one onto feature-map ids F01–F07: both parse entries; four built-in schemas; mapping-container replacements; YAML 1.1 extras and merge keys; dump presentation; custom tags; nesting, alias, and merge budgets. Finite sets are enumerated: Failsafe/JSON/Core/YAML 1.1; Core/JSON/Failsafe tags !!null/!!bool/!!int/!!float/!!str/!!seq/!!map; YAML 1.1 extras !!binary/!!timestamp/!!set/!!omap/!!pairs; merge key <<; YAML 1.1 boolean words. Named oracles match the sealed suite and the ground-truth library: answer: 42 as number 42; empty versus multi-document contrast; alias identity including recursive default sequence; later-wins under json; Failsafe versus Core versus JSON versus YAML 1.1 implicit rules; __proto__ as an own property; real-map numeric versus string keys; empty !!binary as empty bytes and invalid Base64 as a throw; merge off under Core and on under YAML 1.1; dump quoting of yes/true/42/null and ---; custom !point/!space; ten nested sequences at limit 20 versus 5; default merge budget 10000 versus 10001. Layout is disclosed: library with package.json at the built root, ESM artifact from exports["."].import or module, CPU-only, Node.js LTS plus npm, no native extensions. Preamble obligations before the first FP heading (Core default load, YAML 1.1-extended default dump quoting, real from-source artifact, no JSON-only proxy, limits for untrusted input, JavaScript-only tags out of scope) are graded by the matching feature suites rather than left as untested prose.

gt_core_logic.rationale: Ground-truth is a real TypeScript library (event parse, constructor, schema and tag tables, dump presenter), not stubs: named exports load/loadAll/dump, four Schema values, defineScalarTag/defineSequenceTag/defineMappingTag, withTags, and attachable map/merge tags. produce_sft is off, so excerpt-versus-original is out of scope. Every non-scaffolding feature records verification.status passed, gt_verified true, and red_check probe-ok from B-loop probes. This-run suite --all --world neutral collected 506 items and exited 0, matching D's d_verify_evidence (506 passed, exit 0) and accept_cursor status complete. F00 is scaffolding.

artifact_consistency.rationale: Product symbols the suite actually invokes (load, loadAll, dump, Schema, FAILSAFE_SCHEMA, JSON_SCHEMA, CORE_SCHEMA, YAML11_SCHEMA, withTags, defineScalarTag, defineSequenceTag, defineMappingTag, mapTag, realMapTag, legacyMapTag, mergeTag, and parse/dump option keys filename/json/schema/maxDepth/maxAliases/maxTotalMergeKeys/indent/flowLevel/seqNoIndent/seqInlineFirst/skipInvalid/sortKeys/lineWidth/noRefs/quoteStyle/forceQuotes/flowBracketPadding/flowSkipCommaSpace/flowSkipColonSpace/quoteFlowKeys/tagBeforeAnchor) are named on the Interface Contract surface with the call shapes the driver uses. extra_tags is a harness-only list of export names; the driver attaches them with withTags before the product sees the options object, matching the Contract attach operation. The objective-gate and Stage F contract-coverage-gap warning lists collections.abc, os, os.environ, pytest, and sys. Those strings occur only as Python harness imports in the hidden suite (conftest, shared driver, Sequence typing, and parametrize); they are not product API. Adding them to the Contract would mis-specify a JavaScript library. They must not be added. The gate's 'already named in the Contract' exception does not apply because these are not product members; the gap is a false positive of comparing a Python-stdlib inventory to a JS library Contract. This repair round therefore acquits the warning rather than routing spec_repair. test_usage names/imports are empty because observations go through a spawned Node driver, not Python product imports. test_manifest lists seven acceptance files plus harness support, workdir ".", and execution_groups F01–F07. A shared helper module lives beside the driver in the sealed tests tree and is imported by every feature file; this-run isolated collection of 506 proves it ships with the suite. Suite honesty is d_verify_evidence (506 passed, exit 0) plus accept_cursor status complete, plus this-run isolated green. Published test_command on the sealed manifest is the pytest invocation that D and this review ran. B-direct published runner truth is that test_command plus mapped install/build (Node dist tarball pin, npm ci, npm run build against the neutralized package.json).

leakage.rationale: The objective gate reported no test-reference-leak and no runner-identity-leak. Identity on the published surface was already judged by the dedicated leak pass; this review does not re-run substring matching. Public PRD, Contract, and Hardware_Requirements use the neutralized product vocabulary ymlcodec. Hidden tests do not quote test file names or path::test_node ids in public documents. Published install/build pins are a nodejs.org dist tarball plus npm ci; they do not embed a blacklisted identity inside a URL. Hardware_Requirements describes contestant-machine toolchain floors only (Node.js LTS, npm, CPU, from-source bundle) and does not name pipeline-internal paths.

test_focus.rationale: Acceptance files target PRD core capabilities per feature point: parse/empty/multi-document/alias/duplicate-key/quoting/malformed (F01), four-schema implicit and explicit type resolution (F02), plain/real/legacy maps and __proto__ (F03), YAML 1.1 binary/timestamp/set/omap/pairs/merge (F04), dump quoting/presentation/refs/unrepresentable (F05), custom scalar/sequence/mapping tags and attach rules (F06), nesting/alias/merge budgets (F07). Assertions are constructed values, types, identity, dump text, and classified parse/dump failure — not log strings, private parser internals, or bundle trivia. CLI is not graded and is not a feature-point suite.

test_correctness.rationale: Recorded B-loop probes killed wrong implementations on every feature. Credited F01 kill: ints_as_strings (implicit Core 42 stays a string) died on tests/F01_acceptance.py::test_answer_42_is_number_under_default_core; adversarial/F01/verdict.json records probes_killed 24 with 0 survived, including load_empty_succeeds, alias_deep_copy, keep_first_duplicate, and first_line_always. Parallel feature records kill failsafe_uses_core, proto_pollutes, core_also_merges, never_quote, ignore_custom_tags, and ignore_alias_budget. Mutant directories are absent; discrimination is the recorded probe kills, which the b-direct rule accepts via red_check_source b-loop-probes. Negative arms use semantically invalid inputs (empty stream on load, unknown tags, malformed YAML, over-budget nests/aliases/merges, functions on dump). require_parse_failure / require_dump_failure assert ok is False and a non-null error payload — the Contract carrier that a failed parse or dump throws and yields no usable document — not absence of success alone. Whole-suite mechanical flags that look like negatives are either (1) positive value oracles that a Core integer is the number 42 rather than the string 42, (2) that throw-and-no-document carrier, (3) success-path empty multi-document lists the PRD names, or (4) skip/omit and no-reuse contrasts that also assert remaining constructed values or two separate objects. The suite cannot stay green without the locally built ESM artifact: every library call goes through the Node driver. No pytest skip/xfail. Tests do not import private TypeScript modules; the driver calls named exports. This-run isolated neutral suite collected 506 and exited 0.

prd_coverage.rationale: coverage_matrix features F01–F07 list core capabilities with test_files pointing at the matching acceptance file; the capabilities[] inventory marks every listed capability core_covered. Each core family has a recorded probe kill, not smoke-only coverage. The mandatory substrate is a real from-source bundle loaded into Node; value equality is against constructed JS values from that artifact. There is no approved cheaper proxy (JSON-only parser, always-string scalars, or dump-as-JSON). The cpu_baseline profile means a real host that can load the locally built artifact; it is not a removable accelerator, and it does not license treating value oracles as weak proxies. F00 is scaffolding (harness/conftest) with verification n/a. A matrix shorthand that groups empty !!binary with invalid Base64 as failing is looser than the PRD (empty is empty bytes; invalid fails); the sealed F04 tests follow the PRD, so the capability is covered rather than weakly proxied. Preamble sentences that a contestant could ignore (Core default on answer: 42; empty vs multi-document contrast; schema switch as the only implicit-rule change; dump quoting of yes under the default dump schema; custom tags via withTags; omitted merge budget 10000 vs 10001) each have a failing assertion in the matching feature file.

design_goal_unity.rationale: PRD, Contract, hidden tests, and ground-truth jointly specify one JavaScript YAML parse-and-dump library (Core default load, YAML 1.1 extras on request, schema-aware dump, custom tags, resource limits). No D_ISSUES_FOR_E or CODE_ISSUES_FOR_D. The Stage F contract-coverage-gap warning is the harness-module inventory already acquitted under artifact_consistency: pytest/os/sys/collections.abc are not product members and must not be added to the Contract. The four bottom lines hold: contestants can rebuild from public materials (entries, option keys, and oracles are on the PRD and Contract surface); a hollow or degraded implementation is killed by recorded probes; published scoring surfaces stay identity-neutral; the sealed pytest command actually runs against the neutralized tree. Per-feature Stage E reviews F01–F07 are passed. This-run isolated neutral suite collected 506 and exited 0, matching D's d_verify_evidence.
